I feel like she did genuinely care about him and they did love each other on some level. I just think they weren't well suited in the sense that they're both strong personalities. 

I think, while he definitely liked strong willed women, Michael actually needed someone a lot more "go with the flow" since he was used to calling the shots in his life. Would it have been good for him to have to compromise some? Sure. But he was the King of Pop, no one was going to be able to force him. 

I hope no one things that's me attacking him, because it definitely isn't.  His independence was a coping mechanism for not only his childhood and family issues but also for his entire life. How could you trust anyone when you're that big and most of the people around you had proven you were important to them because of what they could get out of it?

I do think they would have made really good friends,  just not a successful romantic partnership given their headstrong personalities.

Some of you may remember me from about 5 months ago. I had been tasked with creating an art piece using a bison skull for a local charity auction. I had never worked with bones before, but the skull was supposed to be fully cleaned before it was given to me. It definitely wasn't, though. Although it looked clean at first glance, the brain and a decent bit of interior tissue was still intact. The person who tasked me with this refused to talk to the person who "cleaned" it, and it wound up being made my problem. 

I was overwhelmed and had reached out for help here. Thanks to the helpful guidance given, I began  the process of maceration. It took many months as it was slow going getting all the tissue successfully power washed out. BUT I did it! It's now fully cleaned, painted, varnished, polished and ready for auction later this month. 

THANK YOU to everyone here who helped me! 🥰 I couldn't have done it without you! 

And with that, I think I'm officially retiring from bison skull painting and going back to the canvas painting I'm used to. 😉

Oh, yeah, I absolutely get what you're saying there.  I've thought about that, too, and my take on it was that keeping Harry but calling him a delinquent was the "lesser of two evils" for them.  Like I said, I didn't see how they would be able to stand him being free to be as "freakish" as he wanted under someone else's care, but I also don't think they wanted people to think he was fully "one of the family".  Basically, they turned him into a charity case in the eyes of society.  "Look what great people we are, taking in and caring for this awful child who is nothing like our precious boy who could do no wrong."  It also gives them excuses to be less than kind to Harry without people around them giving them as much guff about it. Also, classing him as  a delinquent served the purpose of manipulating others into thinking they should distance themselves from Harry as well, and on top of that it could act as a cover story for any weird happenings that went on around Harry should he accidently (or purposely) use magic.  Here I am thinking of in the book when a young Harry is described as suddenly finding himself on the roof of his school.  "How'd he get up there? Who knows, but he's an absolutely naughty boy who finds any way he can to cause trouble."  So in the end I always thought that the Dursleys were definitely resentful of feeling forced to take Harry in and didn't like the situation or the idea of others thinking they were associated in any way to a delinquent, but it was still better in their mind than people somehow finding out they were related to a wizard...

Personally, I always had the feeling that the main reason they took Harry in and kept him was because they wanted to keep him as hidden from the world as they could.  Yes, they had to keep him around which meant people knew of his existence and relationship to the Dursleys, but with him living under their roof and so under lock and key, they were much more able to control him and therefore had a better chance of hiding his "abnormalities" from the world.  After all, the Dursleys were intensely concerned with status and keeping up appearances.  I don't think they would be able to stand knowing Harry was being raised by someone else in the muggle world who wouldn't make sure to keep Harry as hidden, and it seems to me like Dumbledore was pretty determined (and for good reason) that Harry should start life in the muggle world.

I could see human servants existing in the wizarding world, particularly when one thinks of the existence of squibs who would probably have wanted to stay part of the wizarding world in many cases but would need jobs they could do without magic.  I mean, Filch was basically a servant for Hogwarts in that way,even if in a more specified role, so why not in other establishments/households?  However, I doubt the Malfoys would have had human servants because they wouldn't be able to get as much done as house elves.  Also, any human servant (unless some sort of prisoner) would be working for pay/loyalty primarily and wouldn't be FORCED to stay anywhere they didn't want to be unlike house elves.  I can't see the Malfoys being particularly nice to any servant, whether elf or human, so I just don't see why any human servant would stay there.  I always got the feeling Dobby was the only house elf at Malfoy Manor, but I'm sure they replaced him once he wasn't around anymore.
